answer: Proof of Space-Time resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to seal a key-bound dataset via a slow hash graph and pass timed Merkle audits each epoch. Because plots cannot be shared or recomputed on time, each fake identity demands dedicated disk space and I/O bandwidth, denying botnets a free haven. Beyond an ivory facade of unique keys, this physical cost stops one host from opening like a lotus into clones, though bulk cloud storage can still fund extra slots.
